title: Juniper and the Contact
premise: Marguerite Brightwater, a crash investigator haunted by the row-twelve accident that killed her family, has spent years maintaining the lie that she was never on that plane. When a stranger named Juniper arrives claiming Marguerite once saved her life — a favor Marguerite has no memory of — she brings a debt: extract Dr. Elias Vann, a defector carrying evidence of a manufactured crash, out of the country before the border checkpoint shifts change at dawn. As they race through checkpoints and betrayals, Marguerite realizes Vann's testimony could prove her family's deaths were no accident, but delivering him may require sacrificing the found family she's built with Juniper's crew. In the end, Marguerite chooses truth over survival, testifying to what happened in row twelve, and discovers the favor was real — her forgotten act of kindness is the only reason any of them are still alive.
about_author: Isandro Eriksen is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accident timelines before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where fog rolls in most mornings, which they insist is excellent for plotting.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She works a routine crash investigation, methodical and numb, then returns home to her packed bag and polished lie about row twelve. A knock reveals Juniper, who thanks her for saving her life on Flight 4471 — a flight Marguerite swears she wasn't on. Emotional beat: the past knocking louder than grief can muffle.

chapters.title: A Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She explains the debt: someone swapped boarding passes in row twelve, and Marguerite's name is on a list of people who 'should have died.' She offers protection in exchange for help extracting defector Elias Vann before the checkpoint shifts change. Emotional beat: vertigo as Marguerite's tidy lie begins cracking open.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She pulls the original crash file against protocol and finds anomalies she flagged years ago were overwritten — seat assignments altered, black-box timestamps shifted. Someone inside the agency buried it. Emotional beat: cold fury replacing grief; the investigator becomes the investigated.

chapters.title: The Crew at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Marguerite meets Juniper's ragged crew — a forger, a retired border guard, a teenage driver named Pip — and resents how easily they feel like family. They plan the extraction route through two checkpoints. Emotional beat: guarded warmth; loyalty offered before trust is earned.

chapters.title: Vann's Condition
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The defector agrees to come, but insists his evidence travels separately — he may be bait, and he knows it. He hints he recognizes Marguerite's name from the manifest manipulation. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into dread as the plan's center of gravity wobbles.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The first crossing goes wrong when a face-recognition flag hits Marguerite's file; the crew improvises, splitting the convoy. Marguerite realizes whoever flagged her knew exactly where she'd be. Emotional beat: terror braided with exhilaration — alive in a way grief never allowed.

chapters.title: What Juniper Owes
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Pressured by her handler, Juniper admits the truth: the 'favor' was engineered, but the debt is real — Marguerite did pull a stranger from wreckage once and forgot. Her handler wants Vann silenced, not saved. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth tearing Juniper down the middle.

chapters.title: The Shift Change
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. With minutes before the checkpoint shifts change, the crew executes a decoy run while Marguerite confronts Vann: he confirms the crash was manufactured, and her family died because of a passenger in row twelve who was never supposed to board. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Climax, dual POV. At the final checkpoint, Juniper turns on her handler, buying Marguerite seconds to move Vann through on foot. Pip is caught; Marguerite goes back for her, choosing the found family over the mission clock. Vann crosses alone. Emotional beat: sacrifice as proof of love, not failure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, weeks later. Vann's evidence lands; hearings begin, and Marguerite finally tells the truth about row twelve — publicly, on record. Juniper's crew gathers at her table, the go-bag unpacked at last. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid in full, and worth it.
